execution_time.meaning: Time at which the selected pending liquidity transaction is included
execution_time.evidence: limit the time of the execution of their pending transactions

user_deadline.meaning: User-intended last permitted execution time; a specification variable, not an assumed existing contract argument

liquidity_operation_completed.meaning: The selected deposit or withdrawal completed without reverting

preconditions.text: The selected pending liquidity transaction is executed after the user's intended deadline.
evidence: transaction would revert at 10:31am if not yet executed
preconditions.derivation: The example contrasts a 10:30am deadline with later execution. The deadline represents user intent even though the report says the API lacks this parameter.

safety.text: A liquidity operation must not complete after the user's specified latest acceptable execution time.
evidence: AMMs should provide their users with an option to limit the time of the execution of their pending transactions when adding and removing liquidity.
With deadline protection if Alice has set deadline = 10:30am, transaction would revert at 10:31am if not yet executed
safety.derivation: Infer an execution-time obligation from the stated user time-limit intent and example. This is not a claim that the current interface already has a deadline.

effects.text: The stale transaction nevertheless completes in the reported scenario.
evidence: At 3pm, market crashes, her transaction executes
effects.derivation: Completion under the stale-time premise captures only the timing effect, not the entire alleged economic impact.

assumptions: The user has a meaningful latest acceptable execution time, which may only exist outside the current contract interface.
Time observations use a common timestamp scale and refer to the same operation.
Other execution requirements are met in the selected scenario.
unresolved: Stage three must decide how externally expressed user intent is bound when the API has no deadline input; do not invent a Solidity variable.
